ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A squid with a mass of $1.4\mathrm{kg}$ is initially at rest in water after inhaling $0.1\mathrm{kg}$ of water. When faced with danger, it expels all of the inhaled water backward in an extremely short time, propelling itself forward with a velocity of $2\mathrm{m/s}$.

1. Determine the magnitude of the velocity $v$ with which the squid expels the water.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A squid with a mass of $1.4\mathrm{kg}$ is initially at rest in water after inhaling $0.1\mathrm{kg}$ of water. When faced with danger, it expels all of the inhaled water backward in an extremely short time, propelling itself forward with a velocity of $2\mathrm{m/s}$. Determine the magnitude of the velocity $v$ with which the squid expels the water.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The squid-plus-inhaled-water system is initially at rest, so its initial total momentum is 0. During the extremely short expulsion, treat the system as isolated and conserve momentum. Take forward as positive. After expulsion, the squid body of mass 1.4 kg moves forward at 2 m/s, and the expelled water of mass 0.1 kg moves backward at speed v in the lab frame. Thus the final momentum is 1.4(2) - 0.1v. Set this equal to zero: 1.4(2) - 0.1v = 0. Therefore 2.8 = 0.1v, so v = 28 m/s.
